title: Nepal .gov.np web-infrastructure observations
description: Passive observations of Nepal's public-sector web infrastructure: the canonical local-level roster, the Certificate Transparency hostname inventory, an evidence-bearing hostname-to-local-level attribution, and per-hostname hosting, DNS, TLS and HTTP behaviour. The unit of record is a hostname, not a local level, because a hostname can belong to an office the roster does not contain; attribution to a local level is a separate join whose method and evidence URL are recorded on every row. Collection uses ordinary public requests only and never scans ports, probes for vulnerabilities, or bypasses robots.txt.
grain: one row per hostname per observation (hosting, DNS, TLS, HTTP headers, robots, scripts, reachability); the roster table is one row per local level, the attribution table one row per level-to-hostname link (an unresolved level appears once with an empty hostname; 47 levels carry a second alias hostname), the entities table one row per apex hostname, the entity_hosting table one row per apex joining owner type to addresses, RDAP operators and reachability, and the sites table one row per discovered hostname

coverage.note: Hostname discovery and per-host observations are a 2026-11-05 snapshot over a 20-hostname pilot sample; attribution, the roster adjudication and manual overrides were extended through 2026-11-09 across all 753 local levels over the 2,837-hostname discovered inventory. The pilot sample is not a census of the discovered hostnames.

sources.name: Office of the Auditor General — local-level report API
Wikidata Query Service — P856 official website
OpenStreetMap Overpass API — Nepal administrative relations

artifacts.description: The discovered .gov.np hostname universe with apex and subdomain decomposition and whether the hostname entered the observation sample.
One row per discovered apex hostname with its classified owning public body, owner type and scope, method and evidence; unknown when no committed source names an owner.
The entity-typed evidence-bearing join: one row per apex with owner type/scope, resolved addresses, RDAP operators and an observed reachability state (reachable, timeout, refused, no_dns, unknown).
One row per hostname-address with DNS status, one TCP state per port 80/443, latency, inverse DNS and the observation time.
One row per observed address with its RDAP allocation holder, registrant handle, country, allocation range and inverse DNS.
Multi-vantage reachability measurements executed through the public Globalping probe network, with the probe country, ASN, network and per-request timings.
Canonical local-level roster as delivered by the OAG API, with stable string identifiers and normalized names.
Hostname-to-local-level links with method, confidence and evidence; unresolved local levels carry an empty hostname.
Resolved addresses, ASN, organization, country evidence and the conservative hosting classification per hostname.
Per-hostname DNS record counts and SPF/DMARC evidence states.
Root-resource response status and presence of six audited security headers per hostname.
Passive TLS handshake observations. Header-only when the live TLS collection has not run: an empty table is unavailable evidence, not a passing result.
One row per referenced script, plus one empty-script row for each hostname whose page was not fetched, so collection failures keep their denominator.
robots.txt availability, status and directive counts per hostname.
The 12 roster records excluded from the canonical 753, each with status, superseding record and evidence.
Full attribution output: one record per mapped local level and one per unresolved local level, with method, confidence, evidence URL, evidence note and decision date.
Manual reject/accept corrections applied after the automatic sources, each with a reason, evidence and decision date.
Full entity classification output: one record per discovered apex hostname with owner label, type, scope, method, evidence and the unclassified residual.
The crt.sh response the inventory was derived from, committed because a live query cannot be reproduced byte-for-byte.
Primary attribution source: the 753-row local-body e-office directory with English name, wards and website per row.
Secondary attribution source: 1,534 Wikidata items with a P856 official website, used only when the name and district agree.
Corroboration source: 749 OSM administrative relations, of which 5 carry a website tag.
Curated apex hostnames whose owner is citable but absent from Wikidata P856; used as the manual, highest-confidence entity classification.
Passive DNS resolution, one TCP connect per address/port and inverse DNS for the discovered hostnames; a live observation committed because it cannot be reproduced byte-for-byte.
RDAP allocation metadata for every observed address, naming the registry holder rather than inferring an operator.
Multi-vantage reachability measurements from the public Globalping probe network, including probe location, ASN and network.

verification.method: roster reconciled against the official 753 local levels after adjudicating 12 extra records; every active local level is either attributed or explicitly unresolved; attributed hostnames are unique, end in .gov.np, and appear in a committed discovery source; manual rejections stay unlinked and acceptances stay applied; every mapped row carries method, evidence URL and decision date; every discovered apex hostname carries an entity classification, unknown-typed rows carry no guessed method, and local-level entity ids reconcile with the attribution; every entity_hosting row joins to an entity and a reachability state; observation hostnames are checked against the discovery inventory

cli: python -m govweb.cli globalping kathmandu.gov.np aadarshakotwalmun.gov.np --locations NP IN DE

license.data: MIT; derived from public government and Certificate Transparency responses, attribution required

notes: The 20-hostname observation sample is a deterministic lexicographic pilot, not a census of the 2,837 discovered hostnames or the 753 local levels.
Attribution is not proof of administrative ownership: it records the best available source agreement, with the method and evidence URL on every row.

The local-body directory contains duplicate rows and some wrong or generic links; a row is accepted only when its hostname is a plausible .gov.np local-level name and is not already owned by another local level.
Unresolved local levels are evidence of missing data, not evidence that the local level has no website.
Manual corrections are recorded in attribution_overrides.json so a reviewer can see every deviation from the automatic result.
Non-local government agencies and province portals are not attributed to a local level even when their names collide.
A failed or missing observation is never treated as a secure configuration.
Country-level IP geolocation is approximate and does not establish the physical server location or the hosting contract.
robots.txt directives are publisher instructions, not access control; robots-disallowed hostnames retain no script data.
